sections.title: Words for your phone
sections.content: *telefon* is the word you know from A1. In everyday talk Hungarians also say *mobil*, and it takes the endings you know: *a mobilom* ("my phone"), *a mobilt* ("the phone" as an object). Two phrases belong to a phone all day. *Nincs térerő.* means "There is no signal" (literally "no signal strength"), and *Lemerült a mobilom.* means "My phone has run out of battery". With *lemerül* the phone is the thing that something happens to: nobody runs it down. You know *töltő* ("charger") from Unit 31, so a whole problem fits in two sentences: *Lemerült a mobilom. Van nálad töltő?*

sections.title: Key phrases
rows: My phone has run out of battery.
Do you have a charger on you?
I don't have a charger on me.

items.english: My phone has run out of battery.
There is no signal in the metro.

items.spanish: Nincs térerő, ezért nem tudok telefonálni.
items.english: There is no signal, so I can't make a call.
Do you have a charger on you?

sections.content: Say *Lemerült* (past) when the battery is already flat: *Lemerült a telefonom.* The present *lemerül* means it is running down right now. English "my phone is dead" describes a state; Hungarian tells you what happened to it.
